record.original_question: Is the Post Correspondence Problem decidable for unique-equality-continuation instances?

evidence.quote: Is PCP decidable for unique equality continuation in- stances?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and let $\Sigma^*$ denote the free monoid of finite words over $\Sigma$. An instance of the Post Correspondence Problem (PCP) is a finite list of pairs of nonempty words
$$P = \{(u_1,v_1),(u_2,v_2),\dots,(u_n,v_n)\}\subset \Sigma^*\times\Sigma^*,$$
and a solution of $P$ is a finite sequence of indices $i_1,i_2,\dots,i_k\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ (with $k\ge 1$) such that
$$u_{i_1}u_{i_2}\cdots u_{i_k}=v_{i_1}v_{i_2}\cdots v_{i_k}.$$
For words $x,y\in\Sigma^*$, write $x\le y$ if $x$ is a prefix of $y$. Given an instance $P$, call a pair $(x,y)\in\Sigma^*\times\Sigma^*$ with $x\le y$ or $y\le x$ an admissible configuration if it can arise as $(u_{i_1}\cdots u_{i_j},\,v_{i_1}\cdots v_{i_j})$ for some sequence of indices. Say that $P$ is a unique-equality-continuation instance if for every admissible configuration $(x,y)$ with $x\ne y$ there is at most one index $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ such that the configuration obtained after appending $(u_i,v_i)$ remains admissible (i.e., one of the two resulting words is a prefix of the other).

Question: Is there an algorithm that, given a unique-equality-continuation instance $P$ as input, decides whether $P$ has a solution?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not turn up a definitive resolution of decidability of PCP for unique-equality-continuation instances. Related work by Halava, Harju and collaborators establishes decidability of the marked PCP and of PCP for instances with unique blocks, and decidability of the existence of infinite solutions under uniqueness-of-continuation conditions, but the specific question of decidability of PCP for unique-equality-continuation instances does not appear to be settled in the sources found.

status_evidence.title: Extension of the decidability of the marked PCP to instances with unique blocks
status_evidence.snippet: establishes a new and larger class of decidable instances of the PCP, including the class of marked instances
status_evidence.claim: Related decidability results exist for PCP with uniqueness-style restrictions, but not directly for unique-equality-continuation.

status_evidence.title: Decidable Instances of the Post Correspondence Problem (Ackerman)
status_evidence.claim: Surveys of decidable PCP subclasses do not list unique-equality-continuation as resolved.

status_evidence.title: Post correspondence problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: general PCP undecidable; binary PCP and marked PCP decidable
status_evidence.claim: Wikipedia summary of known decidable variants does not include the unique-equality-continuation case.
